correctness.rationale: Convex spectral-width minimization in the finite-dimensional real affine quotient yields stationary intersection of top- and bottom-eigenspace expectation convex hulls. Toeplitz–Hausdorff replaces convex combinations with pure eigenvectors when at most two observables are present, realizing the sharp 2-distance equality with orthogonal maximizers. For three Pauli blocks the exact radial shells and their overlap yield a sharp 4r/(1+r) formula; two-block spectral radii give constant operator distance 1. Exact rational and direct complex-vector supplementary assertions pass; none prove the general theorem by enumeration.

value.rationale: Provides the sharp and attainable quantitative stability version of a new numerical-information affine rigidity question, identifies two observations as the exact universal convexity threshold, and displays a continuous family with arbitrarily small or zero observation-fiber defect at fixed strictly positive operator distance. The explicit nonlinear information factorization and sharp parameter law explain an intrinsic structural distinction not obtainable from a lone arbitrary counterexample.
